g.data-note: The cooperative path. Nothing on the Go stack is consumed.
g.text: panic(v) inside an opcode handler
pushPanic records the Exception, unwinds to the
last call frame, pushes OpPanic2 and
OpReturnCallDefers

g.data-note: Machine.Panic or a direct panic with an Exception deep in values.go. The iterative-recovery record explains why.
g.text: A Go panic carrying an Exception
from the value layer: runOnce recovers it and Run
takes the same path, so half a million panicking
defers cannot crash the node

g.data-note: doOpReturnCallDefers pops each Defer and runs it like a call.
g.text: the frame's deferred calls run, one at a
time

g.data-note: The Go rule: only a direct call from the deferred function sees the exception.
g.text: recover() called directly by a deferred
function?

g.data-note: Recover returns the exception value and clears it. Exceptions chain to the previous one when a defer panics again.
g.text: exception cleared; the function returns
normally

g.data-note: The unwinding continues frame by frame, each one running its deferred calls first.
g.text: OpReturnCallDefers pops the frame
and re-raises in the caller. The next frame up
runs its own defers: back to the top.

g.data-note: A panic that crosses a realm boundary is never recoverable by the caller. Tests use revive to observe the abort.
g.text: Realm boundary reached
the transaction aborts with UnhandledPanicError,
unless a revive frame catches it. No caller
recovers it, so one realm cannot catch another's
refusal and retry.

svg.text: On gno.land a bounded printer renders the latest exception alone, with no user methods, 1024 bytes at most.
Elsewhere every chained exception prints, oldest first, and String and Error run, at 4 gas per output byte.
A panic while package variables initialize has no call frame to unwind to and fails the message at once. A
Stacktrace keeps 128 calls with the middle elided.
